successCriteria.description: Re-running `semgrep scan --config auto` against src/modules/policy/policy.routes.ts yields zero CWE-79 (XSS) findings on the success-response send calls previously flagged at lines 32, 55, and 97.

The success response body for the GET-by-id, GET-by-leaveType, and PUT handlers is built as an explicitly-constructed object (not the raw service return value passed directly to reply.send), so no user-controlled path param or request body value reaches the response without an explicit construction step that breaks the taint flow.

The JSON response body returned by each of the three fixed handlers is field-equivalent to the prior LeavePolicy projection — no fields added, removed, or type-coerced relative to the object the handler returned before the fix.
All five route paths registered by policyRoutes remain identical to the pre-fix set: /policies, /policies/:id, /policies/type/:leaveType, POST /policies, PUT /policies/:id.

HTTP status codes are unchanged for every handler: 200 for successful GET and PUT, 201 for POST create, 404 for not-found, 400 for invalid leave type or missing required fields, 500 for caught internal errors.

The error-handling structure is unchanged: every handler retains its try/catch, request.log.error on caught errors, and static-string error response bodies ({ error: '...' }) with no user-input reflection.
npm run build (tsc --noEmit under strict mode) succeeds with no type errors and npx jest --passWithNoTests passes with no regressions in existing tests.

constraints: Only src/modules/policy/policy.routes.ts may be modified for this fix. The balance module (src/modules/balance/*), uptime routes (src/modules/uptime/uptime.routes.ts), policy.model.ts, policy.service.ts, policy.repository.ts, and policy.repository.interface.ts must remain untouched.
Do not change any route path or HTTP method registration. Do not change any status code (200/201/404/400/500) or the conditions under which each is returned.

Do not change the error-handling structure: keep the try/catch blocks, request.log.error calls, and static-string error response bodies unchanged. Static error responses are not flagged and must not be altered.
The fix must use Fastify's reply.send() (or reply.status().send()) to emit responses — this is a Fastify codebase, not Express. Do not introduce Express res.json/res.send calls.
Strict TypeScript must remain satisfied (no implicit any, strict null checks). No use of `any` (HARNESS.json no-any rule); use typed objects or `unknown` with type guards where needed.

The response body for the three fixed handlers must remain JSON-serializable and field-equivalent to the LeavePolicy projection the handler previously returned — the fix changes how the body is constructed, not its shape or content.

Do not introduce HTML rendering, template strings, or manual escaping. Fastify reply.send() already serializes objects to JSON with Content-Type application/json; the fix is to break the user-input-to-response taint flow via explicit object construction, not to add HTML escaping.
outOfScope: Modifying the balance module (src/modules/balance/*) — it has no routes file and no reply.send calls; it is unaffected by the CWE-79 pattern.
Modifying the uptime routes (src/modules/uptime/uptime.routes.ts) — same reply.send pattern but not flagged by Semgrep because there is no user-input reflection path.
Adding RBAC/auth middleware to the policy routes (GP-005) — no auth middleware exists on these routes currently and adding it is outside this security-fix phase's scope.
Adding audit logging to the policy routes (GP-002) — the policy routes currently have no audit integration; this is a separate concern from the XSS fix.
Changing the LeavePolicy model, PolicyService, repository, or repository interface — the fix is confined to response construction in the routes file.
Adding new route-level integration tests for policyRoutes — no such tests exist currently and scaffolding them is outside this targeted fix phase. Existing repository unit tests must not regress.

entityInvariants.invariant: Every successful GET-by-id, GET-by-leaveType, and PUT response must project a LeavePolicy object whose fields match the LeavePolicy interface contract (id, policyName, leaveType, entitlementDays, accrualRate, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays, requiresManagerApproval, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt) with no fields dropped, added, or type-coerced relative to the pre-fix response.

The policyRoutes registration function must continue to register exactly the same five route handlers on the FastifyInstance with the same paths and methods; the module's public export signature (async function accepting FastifyInstance) must not change.

interfaceConstraints.operation: GET single policy by id — success response
interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth middleware currently enforced on this route; this phase does not add or remove auth.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns 404 with a static { error: 'Policy not found' } body when the service returns null; returns 500 with a static { error: 'Internal Server Error' } body on a caught exception. These error paths and their static bodies must remain unchanged.

interfaceConstraints.operation: GET policy by leave type — success response
interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth middleware currently enforced on this route; this phase does not add or remove auth.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns 400 with a static { error: 'Invalid leave type' } body when the leaveType param is not a valid LeaveType enum value; returns 404 with a static { error: 'Policy not found for this leave type' } body when the service returns null; returns 500 with a static { error: 'Internal Server Error' } body on a caught exception. These error paths and their static bodies must remain unchanged.

interfaceConstraints.operation: PUT update policy by id — success response
interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth middleware currently enforced on this route; this phase does not add or remove auth.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns 404 with a static { error: 'Policy not found' } body when the service returns null; returns 500 with a static { error: 'Internal Server Error' } body on a caught exception. These error paths and their static bodies must remain unchanged.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The explicitly-constructed success response object for the GET-by-id, GET-by-leaveType, and PUT handlers must match the LeavePolicy interface field set and types defined in src/modules/policy/policy.model.ts — no fields added, removed, or re-typed.

The fix must not alter the PolicyService method signatures or return types (getById, getByLeaveType, updatePolicy) defined in src/modules/policy/policy.service.ts. The routes file consumes these methods unchanged; only the way their return value is mapped into the response body changes.
The policyRoutes export consumed by src/app.ts (app.register(policyRoutes)) must remain a single async function accepting a FastifyInstance — the registration call in app.ts must not need to change.

The leaveType validation in the GET-by-leaveType handler must continue to validate against the LeaveType enum values defined in src/shared/types/index.ts (annual/sick/emergency/unpaid/maternity/paternity) using Object.values(LeaveType).includes(...), unchanged by this fix.

The fix must clear the Semgrep CWE-79 findings under the exact scan configuration used in CI: `semgrep scan --config auto` (no custom local ruleset, no --exclude narrowing) as declared in .github/workflows/gestalt.yml. The success criterion is verified against this same command.

integrationPoints.why: app.ts registers policyRoutes via app.register(policyRoutes); the routes module's export signature and registered paths must remain compatible so app.ts needs no change.

The routes file calls service.getById, service.getByLeaveType, and service.updatePolicy; the fix consumes these method return values unchanged and only changes how the result is projected into the response body.
The Semgrep --config auto scan is the gate that produced the three CWE-79 findings; the fix must result in zero CWE-79 findings on this file under that same scan.
